A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same knapsack algorithms, predictions and theoretical framework despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on synthetic instances and Bitcoin prices, including algorithm comparisons and prediction-sensitivity studies in Section 6 and Appendix A.6.

after.justification: v2 reports original synthetic, Bitcoin and Google-cluster-trace experiments, including comparative performance and sensitivity results in Section 6 and Appendix A.7.

M1.justification: PP-b, PP-a, IPA, MIX and Fr2Int retain their decision rules. Indexed state notation in PP-a, expanded explanations and relocation of IPA pseudocode do not change the algorithms.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on Google cluster traces, introducing workload-derived inputs beyond synthetic and financial data. Its reported Bitcoin coverage also expands from 2017–2018 to 2017–2019 (Appendix A.7.1).

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain their comparator sets: the Sentinel synthetic comparison includes PP-a, Fr2Int-PP-a, Sentinel and ZCL; Bitcoin includes the first three. Google extends that existing three-method comparison without introducing a new baseline.

E3.justification: For 10,000 Bitcoin items, the reported item weight changes from 0.0001 to 0.001, increasing total offered weight from 1 to 10 against unit capacity. v2 also introduces a Google-trace instance-construction protocol. These materially change evaluation conditions, although the PDFs do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The new Google experiment tests sensitivity to prediction error across several delta values (Figure A4), extending robustness evidence to workload-derived inputs. Existing studies of value range, critical-item weight, interval width, prediction correctness and trust parameter are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions use CDFs and notched boxplots. v2 introduces no seed reporting, repeated-run counts, significance tests or new uncertainty-estimation procedure; changed boxplot values retain the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Google results show plotted median competitive ratios around 1.15–1.19 for PP-a and Fr2Int-PP-a versus approximately 1.53–1.62 for Sentinel at delta values 0.5–2 (Figure A4). Synthetic and Bitcoin boxplot distributions also change between v1 Figures 3–4 and v2 Figures A2–A3. Bitcoin results use revised conditions, so they do not establish same-setting gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds the matching interval-prediction lower bound (Theorem 3.6) and integral-knapsack impossibility results (Theorems A.1–A.2). It corrects the point lower-bound proof to use min{1, omega}, substantially rewrites PP-a and Fr2Int proofs, and explicitly conditions Theorem 5.2 on maximum item weight. It also specifies an adaptive adversary and restricts Theorem 4.2 to deterministic algorithms.

C1.justification: The central claims about succinct predictions, near-optimal consistency–robustness and fractional-to-integral conversion remain. v2 narrows the trade-off lower-bound statement to deterministic algorithms and explicitly qualifies the integral conversion guarantee. Interval optimality receives greater prominence in the contribution summary.

C2.justification: v2 more explicitly distinguishes assumptions needed for trusted fractional algorithms, robust MIX and integral conversion, and states that learning the predictor is outside scope. It adds interpretations of the synthetic error parameter and suggests that workload-value distributions explain Sentinel's poorer Google-trace performance.

D1.justification: Appendix A.7.1 newly documents uniformly generated prediction intervals for MIX and IPA. It also specifies Google instance construction through duration scaling, resource factors, item counts and weights. The code-access information is unchanged, and neither version supplies hardware or seed details.

R1.justification: The introduction substantially expands positioning against frequency predictions, advice complexity and Pareto-optimal algorithms for simplified knapsack variants, explaining why their guarantees do not transfer. Appendix A.1 adds stochastic and unit-profit knapsack coverage, with new references including Vondrak and Zenklusen and Boyar et al.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and contribution narrative are extensively rewritten around near-optimal trade-offs. Assumptions receive dedicated discussion, proofs are reorganized and rewritten, and most Sentinel and real-data experimental discussion moves from Section 6 into Appendix A.7.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main-text layout, adds a contribution-summary table, and moves IPA pseudocode into the main text. Existing Sentinel comparisons move to the appendix and are redrawn alongside a new Google plot. Retained supplementary plots are redistributed and regrouped, rather than constituting entirely new figures.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses concrete weaknesses in the theoretical account: capped critical-weight reasoning is corrected, PP-a receives explicit feasibility and profit invariants, and Fr2Int's weight condition becomes precise. Added interval and integral lower-bound analyses substantially improve completeness, while Google-trace experiments broaden validation. These gains support a substantial improvement independently of higher reported performance; the changed Bitcoin setup limits direct score comparisons.
